title: Tor criterion for flatness of the opcycles of a flat complex
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, viewed as the structure ring on the one-point site. Let P^\bullet be a cochain complex of A-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] whose terms are flat A-modules [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and let a be an integer. If for every A-module N the ordinary tensor complex P^\bullet\otimes_A N [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] is exact in degree a-1 (equivalently, H^{a-1}(P^\bullet\otimes_A N)=0 [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules]), then the A-module Q=P^a/\operatorname{im}(d^{a-1}) is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.59.2 (Tag 0653; label more-algebra-lemma-last-one-flat), the Tor_1 argument of its proof

proof.text: Put Q = P^a/\operatorname{im}(d^{a-1}). The homological Tor argument for the short exact sequence defining this cokernel, using that every P^i is flat, gives a natural surjection H^{a-1}(P^\bullet\otimes_A N) \twoheadrightarrow \operatorname{Tor}_1^A(Q,N) for every A-module N [lem-pc-module-opcycles-tor-surjection].

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.59.2 (Tag 0653), Tor_1 argument in the proof

proof.text: By the hypothesis, H^{a-1}(P^\bullet\otimes_A N)=0 for every N, so Step 1 gives Tor_1^A(Q,N)=0 for every N; in particular Tor_1^A(Q,A/I)=0 for every ideal I of A.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.59.2 (Tag 0653), Tor_1 argument in the proof

proof.text: Apply the flatness criterion [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tor-ideal-criterion] to Q. The vanishing from Step 2 is exactly its Tor_1 hypothesis for every ideal quotient, hence Q is flat over A.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00M5 (flatness characterized by Tor_1 of ideal quotients)
